tagline: Through the canyon's rock layers, signed one by one.
intro: North of Shoshoni, US 20 runs past Boysen Reservoir, with the bare yellow and red rock of the Owl Creek Mountains beyond, and enters Wind River Canyon on the Wind River Indian Reservation, which the Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho share. The walls rise as much as 2,500 feet. At three road tunnels the canyon narrows into Precambrian rock, and signs beside the highway name each layer on the way through.
The river was here before the mountains, holding its course while they rose around it. The road came through between 1922 and 1924, replacing the route over Bird's Eye Pass.

moments.title: Boysen Dam
moments.text: At the head of the canyon a rockfill dam holds back Boysen Reservoir, and the railroad passes beneath it through a tunnel 7,131 feet long.

moments.title: Wind River Canyon
moments.text: In 1995, 43 bighorn sheep came from Dubois in horse trailers and rode the last seven miles on railroad flatcars before they were let go along the canyon.

moments.title: Wedding of the Waters
moments.text: At the north end of the canyon the Wind River becomes the Bighorn, changing its name without changing its course.
